  verifiedBy    User?     @relation("SupplierVerifier", fields: [verifiedById], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)
  createdAt     DateTime  @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt     DateTime  @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
  workspace     Workspace @relation(fields: [workspaceId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  aliases       SupplierAlias[]

  @@unique([workspaceId, normalizedKey])
  @@index([workspaceId, iban])
  @@map("suppliers")
}

/// A5.4: one known alternative spelling of a supplier, stored pre-normalized so lookup is a
/// single equality. `source` records how it was learned: "mined" (from FieldCorrection /
/// CodingCorrection override pairs, lib/suppliers/mine-aliases.ts), "manual", or later phases'
/// "vies" | "registry" | "bank".
model SupplierAlias {
  id              String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  workspaceId     String   @map("workspace_id") @db.Uuid
  supplierId      String   @map("supplier_id") @db.Uuid
  aliasNormalized String   @map("alias_normalized")
  source          String   @default("mined")
  createdAt       DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  workspace       Workspace @relation(fields: [workspaceId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  supplier        Supplier  @relation(fields: [supplierId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@unique([workspaceId, aliasNormalized])
  @@index([supplierId])
  @@map("supplier_aliases")
}

/// A6.1: one row per inbound email processed for a workspace — including mail that produced zero
/// documents, which previously vanished without a trace. `outcome` is "ingested" (≥1 attachment
/// or body accepted), "no_document" (nothing ingestable — the case a person should hear about),
/// or "sender_rejected". `bodyPreview` is a short plain-text excerpt kept so a no_document alert
/// can show what the mail actually said without re-fetching anything from the provider.
model InboundEmailIntake {
  id              String    @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  workspaceId     String    @map("workspace_id") @db.Uuid
  fromAddress     String    @map("from_address")
  subject         String?
  bodyPreview     String?   @map("body_preview")
  attachmentCount Int       @default(0) @map("attachment_count")
  acceptedCount   Int       @default(0) @map("accepted_count")
  rejectedCount   Int       @default(0) @map("rejected_count")
  outcome         String
  createdAt       DateTime  @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  workspace       Workspace @relation(fields: [workspaceId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([workspaceId, createdAt])
  @@index([workspaceId, outcome])
  @@map("inbound_email_intakes")
}

/// A3.7 bank-match memory. When a reviewer confirms a bank line -> document (or supplier +
/// coding) match, the DESCRIPTOR PATTERN (normalizeBankDescriptor's residue) is remembered so
/// the next statement line with the same residue gets a priority hint. Cross-supplier hit
/// counts drop rarely-confirmed patterns from the top of the queue. workspaceId is carried
/// directly for RLS.
model BankMatchMemory {
  id             String    @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  workspaceId    String    @map("workspace_id") @db.Uuid
  descriptorKey  String    @map("descriptor_key")
  supplierId     String?   @map("supplier_id") @db.Uuid
  /// Free-text coding hint if the accepted match had one — replayed onto the next matching
  /// document when the confidence is high enough.
  codingHint     Json?     @map("coding_hint")
  hitCount       Int       @default(1) @map("hit_count")
  lastUsedAt     DateTime  @default(now()) @map("last_used_at")
  createdAt      DateTime  @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  workspace      Workspace @relation(fields: [workspaceId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@unique([workspaceId, descriptorKey])
  @@index([workspaceId, hitCount])
  @@map("bank_match_memory")
}

/// A4.4 golden-task injection. A GoldenDocument is a document whose ground-truth fields are
/// known (typically seeded from the extraction-eval fixtures) with one or more DELIBERATELY
/// wrong fields planted. When the review queue serves the workspace's next task, ~5-10% of
/// the time a golden is served instead — the reviewer's correction rate on it is a per-reviewer
/// quality signal (A4.6 dashboard).
model GoldenDocument {
  id             String    @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  workspaceId    String    @map("workspace_id") @db.Uuid
  documentId     String    @unique @map("document_id") @db.Uuid
  /// Field key -> expected correct value. What the reviewer SHOULD land on.
  expectedValues Json      @map("expected_values")
  /// Field key -> the deliberately-wrong value the extraction was overridden to. A subset of
  /// expectedValues' keys; anything not overridden is a straight ground-truth check, not a
  /// planted error.
  plantedErrors  Json      @map("planted_errors")
  isActive       Boolean   @default(true) @map("is_active")
  createdAt      DateTime  @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  workspace      Workspace @relation(fields: [workspaceId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([workspaceId, isActive])
  @@map("golden_documents")
}

/// A4.6 reviewer-quality dashboard. One row per (reviewer, day, action). Rolled up in the
/// dashboard rather than joined against every ReviewTask history entry every render. `outcome`
/// captures the verdict for a golden task (correct/partial/miss) or "reviewed" for a real
/// document; `fieldCount` is how many fields the reviewer changed on this action.
model ReviewerActivity {
  id             String    @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  workspaceId    String    @map("workspace_id") @db.Uuid
  reviewerId     String    @map("reviewer_id") @db.Uuid
  documentId     String?   @map("document_id") @db.Uuid
  goldenId       String?   @map("golden_id") @db.Uuid
  outcome        String
  fieldCount     Int       @default(0) @map("field_count")
  durationMs     Int?      @map("duration_ms")
  createdAt      DateTime  @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  workspace      Workspace @relation(fields: [workspaceId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([workspaceId, reviewerId, createdAt])
  @@index([workspaceId, outcome])
  @@map("reviewer_activity")
}

/// A5.6 reversible supplier merges. A workspace owner merges "Acme Ltd" + "Acme Limited" into
/// one canonical supplier — this table records what was merged into what, with enough state
/// (the losing side's original id, canonicalName, aliases, and the winning side's id at merge
/// time) that /admin can unmerge later and restore the losing row exactly as it was.
model SupplierMergeEvent {
  id                String    @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  workspaceId       String    @map("workspace_id") @db.Uuid
  winnerId          String    @map("winner_id") @db.Uuid
  loserId           String    @map("loser_id") @db.Uuid
  /// The loser's canonicalName + aliases + counters at merge time, serialized so an unmerge can
  /// reconstruct the row without depending on a soft-delete flag or a shadow table.
  loserSnapshot     Json      @map("loser_snapshot")
  /// Null means "still merged"; a set value means an operator unmerged this row on that date
  /// (records the reversal but keeps the audit trail intact).
  revertedAt        DateTime? @map("reverted_at")
  createdById       String?   @map("created_by_id") @db.Uuid
  createdAt         DateTime  @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  workspace         Workspace @relation(fields: [workspaceId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@index([workspaceId, winnerId])
  @@index([workspaceId, loserId])
  @@map("supplier_merge_events")
}

/// A5.9 active-learning: reviewer labels for the pair (supplierA|supplierB). pairId is a
/// stable string ordered by supplier id, so a re-shown pair upserts onto its previous label
/// rather than creating a second row.
model SupplierMatchLabel {
  id             String    @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  workspaceId    String    @map("workspace_id") @db.Uuid
  pairId         String    @map("pair_id")
  sameSupplier   Boolean   @map("same_supplier")
  score          Float
  labelledById   String?   @map("labelled_by_id") @db.Uuid
  createdAt      DateTime  @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt      DateTime  @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
  workspace      Workspace @relation(fields: [workspaceId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@unique([workspaceId, pairId])
  @@index([workspaceId, sameSupplier])
  @@map("supplier_match_labels")
}

/// Cached FX rates. Every provider publishes at most one rate per pair per business day, so this
/// row is keyed on (base, quote, effectiveDate) — the same-day cache hit turns 200 EUR invoices
/// from one workspace into one API call. Cross-workspace: rates aren't tenant data, one row
/// serves everyone. `rate` is the price of 1 unit of `base` in units of `quote` (EUR/USD 1.0891 =
/// one euro buys 1.0891 US dollars). See lib/fx/rates.ts.
model FxRate {
  id            String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  base          String
  quote         String
  effectiveDate DateTime @map("effective_date") @db.Date
  rate          Decimal  @db.Decimal(20, 10)
  source        String
  fetchedAt     DateTime @default(now()) @map("fetched_at")

  @@unique([base, quote, effectiveDate], name: "fx_rates_base_quote_date_key")
  @@index([effectiveDate])
  @@map("fx_rates")
}

/// Ticket #95 (map #35, decision #42): one row per (workspace, monthly close period). Period
/// identity is (periodYear, periodMonth) — monthly cadence — and `vatPeriodEnd` is stamped at
/// open time from the jurisdiction pack's `filings` topic (both ZA VAT201 and LS VAT-12 are
/// monthly today, so vatPeriodEnd flips true on every open when the pack has a `filings`
/// block). State is 'open' | 'locked'; reopen flips 'locked' → 'open' rather than creating a
/// new row, and the sequence-of-events truth lives in audit_events (close.opened /
/// close.period.locked / close.period.reopened / close.period.relocked).
///
/// The lock snapshot is a `lockSnapshot` JSON column carrying `{packCode, packVersion,
/// lockedAt, workspaceModeAtLock, reviewerOfRecord}` (#79). New fields are added to the
/// TypeScript shape in `lib/close/types.ts` without a Prisma migration; a data back-fill
/// migration is only needed when historical rows must gain a required field (as #79 did).
/// Computation (#96) writes into CloseItem.computedValue; sign-off
/// (#97) writes into CloseItem.signedAt/signedById. This ticket owns the persistence and the
/// four lifecycle actions only.
model Close {
  id                 String       @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  workspaceId        String       @map("workspace_id") @db.Uuid
  /// Calendar year of the closing period, e.g. 2026.
  periodYear         Int          @map("period_year")
  /// Calendar month of the closing period, 1-12 (Jan = 1).
  periodMonth        Int          @map("period_month")
  /// 'open' (default at creation) or 'locked'. A reopen returns a locked close to 'open';
  /// a relock returns it to 'locked'. History lives in audit_events, not extra columns.
  state              String       @default("open")
  /// True if the workspace's jurisdiction pack declares a VAT `filings` topic and this month
  /// is a VAT-period-end month. ZA VAT201 and LS VAT-12 are both monthly today so this stays
  /// true for every month while the pack has filings; the field exists so a future bi-monthly
  /// jurisdiction can flip it off on non-return months without changing the caller.
  vatPeriodEnd       Boolean      @default(false) @map("vat_period_end")
  /// Jurisdiction pack code/version captured at lock time — null while the close is open.
  /// Together with `lockSnapshot` they are #79's extension surface.
  packCode           String?      @map("pack_code")
  packVersion        String?      @map("pack_version")
  openedAt           DateTime     @default(now()) @map("opened_at")
  openedById         String?      @map("opened_by_id") @db.Uuid
  lockedAt           DateTime?    @map("locked_at")
  lockedById         String?      @map("locked_by_id") @db.Uuid
  lastReopenedAt     DateTime?    @map("last_reopened_at")
  lastReopenedById   String?      @map("last_reopened_by_id") @db.Uuid
  reopenReason       String?      @map("reopen_reason")
  /// Written by lockClose/relockClose per `CloseLockSnapshot` in lib/close/types.ts:
  /// `{ packCode, packVersion, lockedAt, workspaceModeAtLock, reviewerOfRecord }`. Historical
  /// rows locked before #79 landed are back-filled to workspaceModeAtLock='firm' +
  /// reviewerOfRecord=null by 20260912030000_backfill_close_lock_snapshot_mode.
  lockSnapshot       Json?        @map("lock_snapshot")
  createdAt          DateTime     @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt          DateTime     @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  workspace          Workspace    @relation(fields: [workspaceId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  openedBy           User?        @relation("CloseOpener", fields: [openedById], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)
  lockedBy           User?        @relation("CloseLocker", fields: [lockedById], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)
  lastReopenedBy     User?        @relation("CloseReopener", fields: [lastReopenedById], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)
  items              CloseItem[]

  @@unique([workspaceId, periodYear, periodMonth])
  @@index([workspaceId, state])
  @@map("closes")
}

/// One row per checklist line for a given Close. `kind` selects the descriptor from
/// lib/close/item-sets.ts ('bank-recon', 'ap-aging', 'unposted-bill-accruals', 'vat-workpaper',
/// 'cross-border-review'); the descriptor is authored in-repo and materialized as an item at
/// openClose time — a re-open never rewrites existing items and only inserts newly-added
/// descriptors so any historical rows stay attributable to their sign-off.
///
/// `state` is 'pending' | 'signed' | 'override'; only #97 flips signed. `reSignRequired` is
/// set true by reopenClose so the sign-off surface can force a fresh sign — the ticket calls
/// this "marks affected items re-sign-required". Computation (#96) fills computedAt /
/// computedValue; this ticket persists the columns and leaves them null.
model CloseItem {
  id                String   @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  workspaceId       String   @map("workspace_id") @db.Uuid
  closeId           String   @map("close_id") @db.Uuid
  /// Descriptor key from lib/close/item-sets.ts.
  kind              String
  /// Human title snapshotted from the descriptor at open time.
  title             String
  /// Descriptor's `required` flag snapshotted at open time. Required items block relock; the
  /// hard-gate check in #96 is what actually enforces it.
  required          Boolean  @default(true)
  /// Bank recon is "asserted, soft delta" per #42 — a small variance is tolerated instead of
  /// hard-blocking. Copied from the descriptor at open time so a later descriptor change does
  /// not silently rewrite the semantics of an in-flight close.
  softDelta         Boolean  @default(false) @map("soft_delta")
  state             String   @default("pending")
  reSignRequired    Boolean  @default(false) @map("re_sign_required")
  computedAt        DateTime? @map("computed_at")
  computedValue     Json?     @map("computed_value")
  signedAt          DateTime? @map("signed_at")
  signedById        String?   @map("signed_by_id") @db.Uuid
  createdAt         DateTime  @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt         DateTime  @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  workspace         Workspace @relation(fields: [workspaceId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  close             Close     @relation(fields: [closeId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  signedBy          User?     @relation("CloseItemSigner", fields: [signedById], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)

  @@unique([closeId, kind])
  @@index([workspaceId])
  @@map("close_items")
}

/// #207: a bank/financial institution a person has asserted a bank_statement document belongs
/// to (#178's "user asserts, assertion is authoritative" rule — never AI-classified). Distinct
/// from Supplier: an institution issues statements about the workspace's own accounts, it is not
/// a party the workspace pays. `savedLayout` is the reference layout the drift check
/// (lib/checks/statement-layout-drift.ts) diffs every later statement against — null until the
/// first statement for this institution is confirmed, which is a real "not applicable" state,
/// not an absence (#183's inventory requirement).
model Institution {
  id            String     @id @default(uuid()) @db.Uuid
  workspaceId   String     @map("workspace_id") @db.Uuid
  name          String
  normalizedKey String     @map("normalized_key")
  /// {columns: string[], headerLabels: Record<string,string>, dateFormat: string, amountFormat: string}
  /// — see StatementLayout in lib/checks/statement-layout-drift.ts. Page/section structure is
  /// deliberately excluded: too fragile, varies within a single bank's own statements.
  savedLayout   Json?      @map("saved_layout")
  createdAt     DateTime   @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt     DateTime   @updatedAt @map("updated_at")
  workspace     Workspace  @relation(fields: [workspaceId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  documents     Document[]

  @@unique([workspaceId, normalizedKey])
  @@index([workspaceId])
  @@map("institutions")
}

// Deliberately NOT a "use server" module. A "use server" file may only export async functions,
// so `paths`, `NO_ACCESS` and friends cannot live in one — and both actions.ts and
// workspace-actions.ts need them. Extracting them here is the only way to share them.
import { requireWorkspaceRole } from "@/models/workspaces"
import { revalidatePath } from "next/cache"

/** `documents` is only the detail-page prefix — there is no document list page; the sheet is
 * the view of that data, so document mutations revalidate the file's `sheet`. */
export const paths = (workspaceId: string) => ({ overview: `/workspaces/${workspaceId}`, documents: `/workspaces/${workspaceId}/documents`, pipeline: `/workspaces/${workspaceId}/pipeline`, files: `/workspaces/${workspaceId}/worksheets`, dictation: `/workspaces/${workspaceId}/dictation`, templates: `/workspaces/${workspaceId}/settings/templates`, reports: `/workspaces/${workspaceId}/settings/reports`, workspace: `/workspaces/${workspaceId}/settings/workspace`, integrations: `/workspaces/${workspaceId}/settings/integrations`, tax: `/workspaces/${workspaceId}/settings/tax`, review: `/workspaces/${workspaceId}/review`, rules: `/workspaces/${workspaceId}/settings/rules`, modules: `/workspaces/${workspaceId}/settings/modules`, settingsEmail: `/workspaces/${workspaceId}/settings/email`, approvals: `/workspaces/${workspaceId}/automation/approvals`, receipts: `/workspaces/${workspaceId}/receipts`, expenses: `/workspaces/${workspaceId}/expenses`, accounting: `/workspaces/${workspaceId}/accounting`, exceptions: `/workspaces/${workspaceId}/exceptions` })

/** Revalidates the whole workspace segment layout, not just one page — needed whenever a change
 * (module toggle, rename, ownership transfer) should update the persistent sidebar, which the
 * layout renders once and a plain revalidatePath(concretePath) does not reach. */
export const revalidateWorkspaceLayout = () => revalidatePath("/workspaces/[workspaceId]", "layout")

export const sheetPath = (workspaceId: string, fileId: string) => `/workspaces/${workspaceId}/worksheets/${fileId}/sheet`

/** Refusals, spelled out. The generic underscore-to-space fallback turns
 * "member_not_found" into "member not found", which is fine for most codes but not all of them.
 * Codes not listed here still fall through to that behaviour. */
const BILLING_MESSAGES: Record<string, string> = {
  free_trial_storage_exceeded: "You've reached the 200 MB free-trial upload limit for this workspace.",
  fx_rate_pending: "This document is in a different currency and its exchange rate hasn't been fetched yet. Try again in a moment.",
  // Integrations (P1). The url_* codes come from lib/url-safety's SSRF guard.
  integrations_not_available: "Integrations aren't enabled on this deployment.",
  accounting_not_available: "The Bigcapital accounting bridge isn't enabled on this deployment.",
  url_scheme_not_https: "The webhook URL must start with https://.",
  url_private_ip: "That URL points at a private or internal address, which isn't allowed.",
  url_invalid: "That doesn't look like a valid URL.",
  url_has_credentials: "Remove the username and password from the URL.",
  url_dns_failed: "That host couldn't be resolved. Check the URL and try again.",
  invalid_event_type: "One of the selected events isn't recognised.",
  api_key_not_found: "That API key no longer exists.",
  webhook_endpoint_not_found: "That webhook endpoint no longer exists.",
  delivery_not_found: "That delivery no longer exists.",
  // Accounting connectors (P2).
  integration_connection_not_found: "That connection no longer exists.",
  bill_missing_total: "This document has no total to push.",
  ledger_duplicate: "A bill with this reference number already exists in your accounting ledger.",
  bank_match_not_found: "That match no longer exists.",
  inbound_email_disabled_for_clinical: "Inbound email intake isn't available for a healthcare workspace.",
  pattern_invalid: "Enter a full email address (name@domain.com) or a domain (@domain.com).",
  allowed_sender_not_found: "That sender no longer exists.",
  // Dext-parity Phase 3 WP3.1/WP3.2: approval workflows.
  approval_workflow_not_found: "That approval workflow no longer exists.",

content.content:
### Purpose

Resolve one stable target, run two independent assessments, synthesize a design critique, persist a snapshot, and ask the user what to improve next. The chat response is the primary deliverable; the snapshot is an archive of that run.

### Hard Invariants

- Assessment A (design review) and Assessment B (detector/browser evidence) are both required.
- Assessment A and B MUST run as two isolated sub-agents whenever a sub-agent/Task tool is exposed. Running them inline in this context is "possible" but is NOT permitted; it is a degraded run. Inline is allowed ONLY when no sub-agent tool exists (or the user declined, on harnesses that ask).
- If you degrade for any reason, the report's first line MUST be a banner: `⚠️ DEGRADED: single-context (<reason>)`. A silent degraded critique is a failed critique.
- Assessment A must finish before detector findings enter the parent synthesis context. Detector output is deterministic, but it still anchors judgment.
- A skipped detector is a failed critique run unless `impeccable detect` is missing or crashes after a real attempt.
- Viewable targets require browser inspection when available.
- Any local server started only for critique visualization must run in the background, have a recorded stop method, and be stopped before final reporting unless the user asks to keep it.
- Do not claim a user-visible overlay exists unless script injection succeeded and the detector ran in the page.
- The question is the LAST thing in the response. Write the entire report out first, then ask; nothing follows the question. Prose emitted after a structured question is withheld until the user answers it, so a report written after the question reads as if the critique never ran.
- A run that ends with neither the targeted questions nor a literal `Questions skipped: <reason>` line is an incomplete run. The report is not the finish; the close is.

### Setup

1. **Resolve the target** to a concrete file path or URL. Prefer a source path over a dev-server URL when both identify the same surface; ports drift, paths do not.
   - "the homepage" -> `site/pages/index.astro` or `index.html`
   - "the settings modal" -> the primary component file
   - "this page" -> the current URL or source file
2. **Confirm the target slugs cleanly**:
   ```bash
   .claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable critique-storage slug "<resolved-path-or-url>"
   ```
   Every later command also accepts the resolved target directly and derives the same slug internally; never hand-write a slug. If this exits non-zero, skip persistence and trend for this run, but continue the critique.
3. **Read `.impeccable/critique/ignore.md`** if it exists. Drop matching findings silently; it is the only prior-run input critique consumes.

### Assessment Orchestration

Delegate Assessment A and Assessment B to separate sub-agents. They must not see each other's output. Do not show findings to the user until synthesis.

Sub-agent gate (all harnesses):
- Unless a harness-specific gate below overrides this, spawn A and B as two isolated, parallel sub-agents whenever a sub-agent/Task tool is exposed. This is the default and is mandatory; do not run them inline because it is faster.
- "Unavailable" means exactly one thing: no sub-agent/Task tool is exposed in this session (or, on harnesses that ask, the user declined). It does not mean inconvenient.
- If and only if sub-agents are unavailable, fall back sequentially: finish and record Assessment A, then run Assessment B, then synthesize, and emit the degraded banner.
- Whichever path you take, declare it in the report header (see Report header provenance). Skipping sub-agents without the banner is the most common failure of this command.

If browser automation is available, each assessment creates its own new tab. Never reuse an existing tab, even if it is already at the right URL.

### Assessment A: Design Review

Read relevant source files and visually inspect the live page when browser automation is available. Think like a design director.

Evaluate:
- **Design specificity**: Is the composition, interaction, and visual language grounded in this product, or could an unrelated product use it unchanged? Make this judgment before seeing detector output.
- **Holistic design**: hierarchy, IA, emotional fit, discoverability, composition, typography, color, accessibility, states, copy, and edge cases.
- **Cognitive load**: consult the [Cognitive Load Assessment](#cognitive-load-assessment) section below; report checklist failures and decision points with >4 visible options.
- **Emotional journey**: peak-end rule, emotional valleys, reassurance at high-stakes moments.
- **Nielsen heuristics**: consult the [Heuristics Scoring Guide](#heuristics-scoring-guide) section below; score all 10 heuristics 0-4, marking any heuristic the mode-applicability rule allows as `n/a` instead of forcing a number.

Return: design-specificity verdict, heuristic scores, cognitive load, emotional journey, 2-3 strengths, 3-5 priority issues, persona red flags, minor observations, and provocative questions.

### Assessment B: Detector + Browser Evidence

Run the bundled detector and browser visualization evidence. Assessment B is mandatory and must remain isolated from Assessment A until both are complete.

CLI scan:
```bash
.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable detect --json [target]
```

- Pass markup files/directories as `[target]`; do not pass CSS-only files.
- For URLs, skip CLI scan and use browser visualization.
- For very large trees (500+ scannable files), narrow scope or ask.
- Exit code 0 = clean; 2 = findings.
- If the detector entrypoint is missing or fails to load, report deterministic scan unavailable and continue with browser/manual review.

Browser visualization is required for a viewable target when browser automation is available. Use a localhost dev/static URL for local files; avoid `file://` unless the available browser explicitly supports this workflow. Overlay flow:

1. Create a fresh tab and navigate. Prefer the harness's native/browser-canvas screenshot path before hand-rolling a Playwright/Puppeteer script; only fall back to a custom script when no native browser tool is exposed.
2. Preflight mutable injection by setting `document.title` and appending a `<script>` tag. Read-only evaluate APIs do not count.
3. If mutation is unavailable, skip live server, browser presentation, and injection; report fallback signal.
4. If mutation is available, start `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable live-server --background`, present the browser if supported, label `[Human]`, scroll top, inject `http://localhost:PORT/detect.js`, wait 2-3 seconds, read `impeccable` console messages, then stop the live server.
5. For multi-view targets, inject on 3-5 representative pages.

Return: CLI findings JSON/counts, browser console findings if applicable, false positives, and skipped/failed browser steps with concrete reasons.

After Assessment B returns usable CLI findings, reuse them. Do not rerun `impeccable detect` in the parent unless Assessment B failed, was truncated, or omitted count, rule names, or file locations.

### Generate Combined Critique Report

Synthesize both assessments into a single report. Do NOT simply concatenate. Weave the findings together, noting where the LLM review and detector agree, where the detector caught issues the LLM missed, and where detector findings are false positives.

The chat response is the primary user-facing deliverable. Present the full structured critique below in chat; do not replace it with a summary and a link. The persisted snapshot is an archive of that run.

Structure your feedback as a design director would:

#### Report header provenance

The report's first line MUST declare how the assessments were run, so a degraded run is never silent:
- Dual-agent: `Method: dual-agent (A: <agent-id> · B: <agent-id>)`
- Degraded: `⚠️ DEGRADED: single-context (<reason, e.g. no sub-agent tool exposed>)`

#### Design Health Score
> *Consult the [Heuristics Scoring Guide](#heuristics-scoring-guide) section below.*

Present the Nielsen's 10 heuristics scores as a table:

| # | Heuristic | Score | Key Issue |
|---|-----------|-------|-----------|
| 1 | Visibility of System Status | ? | [specific finding or "n/a" if solid] |
| 2 | Match System / Real World | ? | |
| 3 | User Control and Freedom | ? | |
| 4 | Consistency and Standards | ? | |
| 5 | Error Prevention | ? | |
| 6 | Recognition Rather Than Recall | ? | |
| 7 | Flexibility and Efficiency | ? | |
| 8 | Aesthetic and Minimalist Design | ? | |
| 9 | Error Recovery | ? | |
| 10 | Help and Documentation | ? | |
| **Total** | | **??/[applicable max]** | **[Rating band]** |

The applicable maximum is 4 times the number of heuristics you actually scored: **/40** when all ten apply, **/32** when two are `n/a`. Never print `/40` over a partial set.

Be honest with scores. A 4 means genuinely excellent. Most real interfaces score 20-32 out of 40.

**Mode applicability**: heuristics 7 (Flexibility and Efficiency) and 10 (Help and Documentation) may be scored `n/a` on Persuade and Experience surfaces (landing pages, campaigns, portfolios, bodies of work), as may any other heuristic that genuinely cannot apply to the surface under review. Write `n/a` in the Score cell with a one-line reason, and renormalize the total to the applicable maximum (e.g. **24/32** when two heuristics are n/a) so the rating band stays proportional. The persisted snapshot must record the applicable maximum and which heuristics were scored n/a.

#### Design Specificity Verdict

**Start here.** Does the result feel authored for this product, or category-interchangeable?

**LLM assessment**: Your unanchored evaluation of design specificity. Cover overall coherence, structural sameness, category-interchangeable choices, and missed opportunities for product character.

**Deterministic scan**: Summarize what the automated detector found, with counts and file locations. Note any additional issues the detector caught that you missed, and flag any false positives.

**Visual overlays** (if injection succeeded): Tell the user that overlays are now visible in the **[Human]** tab in their browser, highlighting the detected issues. Summarize what the console output reported. If browser visualization was attempted but injection failed, say that no reliable user-visible overlay is available and report the fallback signal instead.

#### Overall Impression
A brief gut reaction: what works, what doesn't, and the single biggest opportunity.

#### What's Working
Highlight 2-3 things done well. Be specific about why they work.

#### Priority Issues
The 3-5 most impactful design problems, ordered by importance.

For each issue, tag with **P0-P3 severity** (see [Issue Severity below](#issue-severity-p0p3) for definitions):
- **[P?] What**: Name the problem clearly
- **Why it matters**: How this hurts users or undermines goals
- **Fix**: What to do about it (be concrete)
- **Suggested command**: Which command could address this (from: /impeccable adapt, /impeccable animate, /impeccable audit, /impeccable bolder, /impeccable clarify, /impeccable colorize, /impeccable critique, /impeccable delight, /impeccable distill, /impeccable document, /impeccable harden, /impeccable layout, /impeccable onboard, /impeccable optimize, /impeccable overdrive, /impeccable polish, /impeccable quieter, /impeccable shape, /impeccable typeset)

#### Persona Red Flags
> *Consult the [Personas reference](#persona-based-design-testing) below.*

Auto-select 2-3 personas most relevant to this interface type (use the selection table in the reference). If `CLAUDE.md` contains a `## Design Context` section from `impeccable init`, also generate 1-2 project-specific personas from the audience/brand info.

### Purpose

Resolve one stable target, run two independent assessments, synthesize a design critique, persist a snapshot, and ask the user what to improve next. The chat response is the primary deliverable; the snapshot is an archive of that run.

### Hard Invariants

- Assessment A (design review) and Assessment B (detector/browser evidence) are both required.
- Assessment A and B MUST run as two isolated sub-agents whenever a sub-agent/Task tool is exposed. Running them inline in this context is "possible" but is NOT permitted; it is a degraded run. Inline is allowed ONLY when no sub-agent tool exists (or the user declined, on harnesses that ask).
- If you degrade for any reason, the report's first line MUST be a banner: `⚠️ DEGRADED: single-context (<reason>)`. A silent degraded critique is a failed critique.
- Assessment A must finish before detector findings enter the parent synthesis context. Detector output is deterministic, but it still anchors judgment.
- A skipped detector is a failed critique run unless `impeccable detect` is missing or crashes after a real attempt.
- Viewable targets require browser inspection when available.
- Any local server started only for critique visualization must run in the background, have a recorded stop method, and be stopped before final reporting unless the user asks to keep it.
- Do not claim a user-visible overlay exists unless script injection succeeded and the detector ran in the page.
- The question is the LAST thing in the response. Write the entire report out first, then ask; nothing follows the question. Prose emitted after a structured question is withheld until the user answers it, so a report written after the question reads as if the critique never ran.
- A run that ends with neither the targeted questions nor a literal `Questions skipped: <reason>` line is an incomplete run. The report is not the finish; the close is.

### Setup

1. **Resolve the target** to a concrete file path or URL. Prefer a source path over a dev-server URL when both identify the same surface; ports drift, paths do not.
   - "the homepage" -> `site/pages/index.astro` or `index.html`
   - "the settings modal" -> the primary component file
   - "this page" -> the current URL or source file
2. **Confirm the target slugs cleanly**:
   ```bash
   .claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable critique-storage slug "<resolved-path-or-url>"
   ```
   Every later command also accepts the resolved target directly and derives the same slug internally; never hand-write a slug. If this exits non-zero, skip persistence and trend for this run, but continue the critique.
3. **Read `.impeccable/critique/ignore.md`** if it exists. Drop matching findings silently; it is the only prior-run input critique consumes.

### Assessment Orchestration

Delegate Assessment A and Assessment B to separate sub-agents. They must not see each other's output. Do not show findings to the user until synthesis.

Sub-agent gate (all harnesses):
- Unless a harness-specific gate below overrides this, spawn A and B as two isolated, parallel sub-agents whenever a sub-agent/Task tool is exposed. This is the default and is mandatory; do not run them inline because it is faster.
- "Unavailable" means exactly one thing: no sub-agent/Task tool is exposed in this session (or, on harnesses that ask, the user declined). It does not mean inconvenient.
- If and only if sub-agents are unavailable, fall back sequentially: finish and record Assessment A, then run Assessment B, then synthesize, and emit the degraded banner.
- Whichever path you take, declare it in the report header (see Report header provenance). Skipping sub-agents without the banner is the most common failure of this command.

If browser automation is available, each assessment creates its own new tab. Never reuse an existing tab, even if it is already at the right URL.

### Assessment A: Design Review

Read relevant source files and visually inspect the live page when browser automation is available. Think like a design director.

Evaluate:
- **Design specificity**: Is the composition, interaction, and visual language grounded in this product, or could an unrelated product use it unchanged? Make this judgment before seeing detector output.
- **Holistic design**: hierarchy, IA, emotional fit, discoverability, composition, typography, color, accessibility, states, copy, and edge cases.
- **Cognitive load**: consult the [Cognitive Load Assessment](#cognitive-load-assessment) section below; report checklist failures and decision points with >4 visible options.
- **Emotional journey**: peak-end rule, emotional valleys, reassurance at high-stakes moments.
- **Nielsen heuristics**: consult the [Heuristics Scoring Guide](#heuristics-scoring-guide) section below; score all 10 heuristics 0-4, marking any heuristic the mode-applicability rule allows as `n/a` instead of forcing a number.

Return: design-specificity verdict, heuristic scores, cognitive load, emotional journey, 2-3 strengths, 3-5 priority issues, persona red flags, minor observations, and provocative questions.

### Assessment B: Detector + Browser Evidence

Run the bundled detector and browser visualization evidence. Assessment B is mandatory and must remain isolated from Assessment A until both are complete.

CLI scan:
```bash
.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable detect --json [target]
```

- Pass markup files/directories as `[target]`; do not pass CSS-only files.
- For URLs, skip CLI scan and use browser visualization.
- For very large trees (500+ scannable files), narrow scope or ask.
- Exit code 0 = clean; 2 = findings.
- If the detector entrypoint is missing or fails to load, report deterministic scan unavailable and continue with browser/manual review.

Browser visualization is required for a viewable target when browser automation is available. Use a localhost dev/static URL for local files; avoid `file://` unless the available browser explicitly supports this workflow. Overlay flow:

1. Create a fresh tab and navigate. Prefer the harness's native/browser-canvas screenshot path before hand-rolling a Playwright/Puppeteer script; only fall back to a custom script when no native browser tool is exposed.
2. Preflight mutable injection by setting `document.title` and appending a `<script>` tag. Read-only evaluate APIs do not count.
3. If mutation is unavailable, skip live server, browser presentation, and injection; report fallback signal.
4. If mutation is available, start `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable live-server --background`, present the browser if supported, label `[Human]`, scroll top, inject `http://localhost:PORT/detect.js`, wait 2-3 seconds, read `impeccable` console messages, then stop the live server.
5. For multi-view targets, inject on 3-5 representative pages.

Return: CLI findings JSON/counts, browser console findings if applicable, false positives, and skipped/failed browser steps with concrete reasons.

After Assessment B returns usable CLI findings, reuse them. Do not rerun `impeccable detect` in the parent unless Assessment B failed, was truncated, or omitted count, rule names, or file locations.

### Generate Combined Critique Report

Synthesize both assessments into a single report. Do NOT simply concatenate. Weave the findings together, noting where the LLM review and detector agree, where the detector caught issues the LLM missed, and where detector findings are false positives.

The chat response is the primary user-facing deliverable. Present the full structured critique below in chat; do not replace it with a summary and a link. The persisted snapshot is an archive of that run.

Structure your feedback as a design director would:

#### Report header provenance

The report's first line MUST declare how the assessments were run, so a degraded run is never silent:
- Dual-agent: `Method: dual-agent (A: <agent-id> · B: <agent-id>)`
- Degraded: `⚠️ DEGRADED: single-context (<reason, e.g. no sub-agent tool exposed>)`

#### Design Health Score
> *Consult the [Heuristics Scoring Guide](#heuristics-scoring-guide) section below.*

Present the Nielsen's 10 heuristics scores as a table:

| # | Heuristic | Score | Key Issue |
|---|-----------|-------|-----------|
| 1 | Visibility of System Status | ? | [specific finding or "n/a" if solid] |
| 2 | Match System / Real World | ? | |
| 3 | User Control and Freedom | ? | |
| 4 | Consistency and Standards | ? | |
| 5 | Error Prevention | ? | |
| 6 | Recognition Rather Than Recall | ? | |
| 7 | Flexibility and Efficiency | ? | |
| 8 | Aesthetic and Minimalist Design | ? | |
| 9 | Error Recovery | ? | |
| 10 | Help and Documentation | ? | |
| **Total** | | **??/[applicable max]** | **[Rating band]** |

The applicable maximum is 4 times the number of heuristics you actually scored: **/40** when all ten apply, **/32** when two are `n/a`. Never print `/40` over a partial set.

Be honest with scores. A 4 means genuinely excellent. Most real interfaces score 20-32 out of 40.

**Mode applicability**: heuristics 7 (Flexibility and Efficiency) and 10 (Help and Documentation) may be scored `n/a` on Persuade and Experience surfaces (landing pages, campaigns, portfolios, bodies of work), as may any other heuristic that genuinely cannot apply to the surface under review. Write `n/a` in the Score cell with a one-line reason, and renormalize the total to the applicable maximum (e.g. **24/32** when two heuristics are n/a) so the rating band stays proportional. The persisted snapshot must record the applicable maximum and which heuristics were scored n/a.

#### Design Specificity Verdict

**Start here.** Does the result feel authored for this product, or category-interchangeable?

**LLM assessment**: Your unanchored evaluation of design specificity. Cover overall coherence, structural sameness, category-interchangeable choices, and missed opportunities for product character.

**Deterministic scan**: Summarize what the automated detector found, with counts and file locations. Note any additional issues the detector caught that you missed, and flag any false positives.

**Visual overlays** (if injection succeeded): Tell the user that overlays are now visible in the **[Human]** tab in their browser, highlighting the detected issues. Summarize what the console output reported. If browser visualization was attempted but injection failed, say that no reliable user-visible overlay is available and report the fallback signal instead.

#### Overall Impression
A brief gut reaction: what works, what doesn't, and the single biggest opportunity.

#### What's Working
Highlight 2-3 things done well. Be specific about why they work.

#### Priority Issues
The 3-5 most impactful design problems, ordered by importance.

For each issue, tag with **P0-P3 severity** (see [Issue Severity below](#issue-severity-p0p3) for definitions):
- **[P?] What**: Name the problem clearly
- **Why it matters**: How this hurts users or undermines goals
- **Fix**: What to do about it (be concrete)
- **Suggested command**: Which command could address this (from: /impeccable adapt, /impeccable animate, /impeccable audit, /impeccable bolder, /impeccable clarify, /impeccable colorize, /impeccable critique, /impeccable delight, /impeccable distill, /impeccable document, /impeccable harden, /impeccable layout, /impeccable onboard, /impeccable optimize, /impeccable overdrive, /impeccable polish, /impeccable quieter, /impeccable shape, /impeccable typeset)

#### Persona Red Flags
> *Consult the [Personas reference](#persona-based-design-testing) below.*

Auto-select 2-3 personas most relevant to this interface type (use the selection table in the reference). If `CLAUDE.md` contains a `## Design Context` section from `impeccable init`, also generate 1-2 project-specific personas from the audience/brand info.

184	  if (q.status === "match") return `Invoiced quantity is within what was ordered${q.allowancePercent > 0 ? ` (the workspace allows ${percent(q.allowancePercent)} over)` : ""}.`

188	  if (others.length) return `${lead} once ${others.map((s) => s.label).join(", ")} ${others.length === 1 ? "is" : "are"} counted${tail}`

209	  if (!value || typeof value !== "object" || Array.isArray(value)) return null

214	    else if (typeof raw === "number" && Number.isInteger(raw) && raw >= 0) out[key] = raw

46:**Purchase Order**:
47-The typed destination for a purchase order, paired with Invoices for matching and cumulative line-item comparison against what has already been invoiced against it.

49-**Receipt**:
50-The typed destination for a receipt. Absorbs expense-claim creation as an action on selected rows rather than as its own destination: Add to claim on the bulk bar (and the pane's overflow for one row) opens a dialog in place, and the claim itself is read and submitted from the receipt's Approval tab. A receipt's own processing state is about its review; whether it sits in a claim is a separate fact, shown in the Claim column.

84-A named, reusable filter/sort/column configuration on a list screen. System views are seeded per screen and are not editable or deletable; a user can duplicate one into an editable, optionally shared, view.

# Critique — Assessment A (Operate mode), ticket #250

## 1. Design-specificity verdict

**The pane is authored; the queues are interchangeable.** The compare row (invoice value, then a muted `PO 100` under it with a boxed `=`/`≠` at the cell's right edge, red only where it is wrong), the sentence-first breakdown that names the sibling invoice ("…once NW-5490 is counted; the workspace allows 5 %"), and the green Match manually band that says what it is comparing against and why ("matched by the PO number on the invoice, not yet confirmed") could only be DocuBite — the arithmetic, the vocabulary (Check, Match manually, Override Mode) and the emerald/red/slate skin are all this product's. The Invoices "Purchase Orders" column and the Purchase Orders queue (Supplier · PO # · Amount · Invoiced · Consumption · Received · State, pills in three colours, a "—" column) would take a competitor's logo without a change. Net: authored where it matters, generic at the list layer.

## 2. Nielsen heuristics (0–4)

| # | Heuristic | Score | Key issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Visibility of system status | 3 | Chip promises 3 `≠`; only 2 are on screen, the third (Total) is below the fold — `invoice-pane-viewpo-1440.png`; `line-match.ts:168-175`. Replace-list candidate click has no busy indicator (`match-manually.tsx:134-139`). |
| 2 | Match with real world | 3 | PO pane says Widget A Remaining **0** when 122 were invoiced against 100 — the over-consumption is hidden by a floor (`po-consumption-panel.tsx:45`, `po-pane-1440.png`). "PO No PO line" under Site survey (`line-items-editor.tsx:92` + prefix at `:136`). |
| 3 | User control & freedom | 2 | Once a per-row picker is changed the only exit is "Save line matches and finish" — no discard, Esc does nothing (`match-manually.tsx:61-68, 77-81`). Chip and sibling-invoice links leave the queue with no `from=` (`po-compare.tsx:59, 200`; `invoice-queue.tsx:125`; `po-consumption-panel.tsx:63`), contradicting #244. |
| 4 | Consistency & standards | 2 | Pane header "3 mismatches" vs two "Mismatch" pills vs tooltip "3 cells do not match"; pill grammar "Matches" (verb) / "Mismatch" (noun) / "Not matched" / "Not compared" (`po-compare.tsx:33-35`); invoice cell "12.5" vs "PO 12.50" (`line-items-editor.tsx:91`); column "Purchase Orders" vs facet "PO" (`invoice-queue.tsx:55, 122`). |
| 5 | Error prevention | 3 | Reject PO has a confirm dialog with consequences and audit note (`match-manually.tsx:144-147`), but it does not say a running Approval will be sent back — that arrives as a toast afterwards (`:45`). |
| 6 | Recognition over recall | 3 | PO value sits directly under the invoice value — good. The red "3" on the chip has no visible meaning, only a `title` (`po-compare.tsx:200`); a dashed chip's meaning is `title`-only (`:188`). |
| 7 | Flexibility & efficiency | 2 | No keyboard path to "next `≠`"; each mismatch needs a mouse click to read the sentence; View PO forces the pane from split to details-only, hiding the source PDF exactly when the reviewer wants to check it (`line-items-section.tsx:102-107`). |
| 8 | Aesthetic & minimalist | 3 | Compare row is calm and quiet. But the PO pane buries Consumption under the incumbent form, a disabled "Save review — Choose a document type first" and a "Conversion pending" banner (`po-pane-1440.png`); the Received column is a column of dashes (`document-queue.tsx:116`). |
| 9 | Error recognition & recovery | 3 | Sentences state allowance and next step ("Approve it in Override Mode with a reason, or fix the match." `line-items-section.tsx:42`); failure toasts say "Nothing changed". Over-by is shown against the allowance while the lead % is against ordered — two bases in one popover (`po-compare.tsx:56-64`). |
| 10 | Help & documentation | 2 | Every explanatory affordance is a `title` tooltip — invisible on touch and to keyboard users: chip, dashed chip, "by hand", Received "—" (`po-compare.tsx:184,188,200`; `line-items-editor.tsx:166`; `document-queue.tsx:116`). |

**Total: 26 / 40.**

## 3. Cognitive load

Decision points with more than four visible options:
- **Match manually band + table** (`invoice-pane-match-manually-1440.png`): Done · Confirm PO-2088 · Replace PO… · Reject PO, plus one native select per row each with N+1 options, plus the underlying cell inputs still editable. Six-plus actions on one panel with no primary/secondary ordering beyond colour.
- **An Invoices row** carries three coloured numbers with three meanings: `PO-2088 ❸` (red, cells), `Needs attention · 1` (amber, checks), `26 Days Away` (blue, aging). The reviewer has to learn that 3 ≠ 1 is not a contradiction.

Checklist failures: no visible legend for `=`/`≠`/dashed chip; the Total `≠` is not in view when the count is; "Not matched" and "Not compared" are near-synonyms as rendered; the PO pane demands a full scroll before the reason for opening it (Consumption) appears.

## 4. Emotional journey

- **Peak**: clicking `≠` and reading "Invoiced quantity is 22 % over what was ordered once NW-5490 is counted; the workspace allows 5 %." with the sibling invoice linked. The reviewer understands the problem in one sentence — this is the surface's promise kept.
- **Valley 1**: that popover lands *on top of* the cell it explains — in `invoice-pane-breakdown-1440.png` "PO 100 ≠" is hidden under the panel's bottom edge. The reviewer loses the thing they clicked.
- **Valley 2**: opening a mismatched row snaps the pane from split to details-only; the source disappears without warning.
- **High-stakes moment (Reject PO)**: the dialog is good — plain consequence, reversibility ("You can choose another PO afterwards"), audit trail. But the second consequence, "the Approval that was running returns to review", only appears as a toast *after* the irreversible-for-the-approver act. Reassurance arrives late.
- **End**: "Line matches saved. Checks re-ran." and the chip turning green or its count dropping is a clean close. On rejection, "PO removed" in the queue is honest.

## 5. Strengths

1. **One source of truth rendered three ways.** `line-match.ts` feeds the queue chip, the pane glyphs and the PO pane; the `=`/`≠` glyph is a `<button>` whose name is the verdict ("Does not match the PO: Quantity, line 1. Show breakdown", `po-compare.tsx:26`) with an `aria-describedby` to the same sentence sighted users read (`line-items-editor.tsx:142`).
2. **Restraint in the compare row.** Matching cells are near-invisible (`text-emerald-700/80`, transparent fill), only `≠` gets red fill and red PO value. Nothing shouts on a clean line; Delivery reads as quiet as it should.
3. **The Match manually band speaks in facts.** "Comparing against PO-2088 · Northwind Traders · $1,565.00 — matched by the PO number on the invoice, not yet confirmed." — provenance and status in one line, the button label changes honestly to "Save line matches and finish" when there is something to save, and the heading takes focus on entry (`match-manually.tsx:37`).

## 6. Priority issues

**P1 — Breakdown popover covers its own anchor.**
What: `Breakdown` positions with a 260px fallback height on first paint and the placement effect only re-runs on `[returnFocusTo, rows.length]` (`po-compare.tsx:112-127`), so the "above" branch computes `rect.top - 260` while the real panel is taller; the panel overlaps the row (`invoice-pane-breakdown-1440.png`). There is also no pointer/arrow tying it to the cell.
Why: the reviewer clicks `≠`, and the value they are questioning vanishes under the explanation.
Fix: measure after mount (ResizeObserver on `panelRef`, or run `place()` in a second `useLayoutEffect` keyed on the panel's `offsetHeight`), add a 8–12px gap, and prefer left/right of the glyph before above; keep the anchored row visible. Add a small caret or a 2px emerald edge on the side facing the glyph.
Impeccable: `layout`.

**P1 — Cross-surface links have no way back (#244).**
What: chip → `/purchase-orders/{id}` (`po-compare.tsx:200`, `invoice-queue.tsx:125`, `line-items-section.tsx:128`), breakdown sibling link (`po-compare.tsx:59`), matched-invoice link (`po-consumption-panel.tsx:63`) all omit `from=`.
Why: an AP reviewer mid-row on invoice 41 of 80 clicks the chip to see the PO, and the Origin link the map promises is absent.
Fix: append `?from=<current path>` on all five `href`s; the queue shell's Origin link then renders.
Impeccable: `harden`.

**P1 — Reject PO dialog hides the send-back consequence.**
What: `match-manually.tsx:145` description says the cells clear and the gate re-evaluates; `sentBack` is only surfaced as a toast at `:45` after the action.
Why: sending a running Approval back is the highest-stakes side effect on this surface; the controller learns of it after they can no longer decline.
Fix: have the summary carry `approvalRunning: boolean`; when true, add a sentence to the dialog — "The Approval that is running will be sent back to review." Same for Replace PO (also sends back).
Impeccable: `clarify` (with Intent `fortify`).

**P2 — The count and the glyphs disagree on screen.**
What: chip "3", header "3 mismatches", but two "Mismatch" pills; the third `≠` (Total) is below the fold (`line-items-section.tsx:58-62`).
Why: the decided rule is "the red count equals the number of `≠` the pane shows" — it is true in code and false in the viewport.
Fix: chip tooltip and header wording → "3 cells · 2 lines + Total"; or scroll the Total's compare line into view when View PO auto-opens; or mirror the Total's `≠` beside the chip.
Impeccable: `clarify`.

**P2 — View PO hides the source, and the suggested state leaves an unreadable table.**
What: comparing flips the pane to details-only (`line-items-section.tsx:102-107`); when there is only a suggestion, nothing widens and at 1440-split the fixed-width table collapses its description column and overprints headers ("DESCRIPTIQUANTITY", `invoice-pane-suggested-1440.png`; `line-items-editor.tsx:225-230`).
Why: the reviewer needs the invoice image beside the PO values; and the suggested-PO row is the one where they most need to read the descriptions to decide.
Fix: keep split at ≥1280 and let the table scroll horizontally with a sticky description column; below that, widen. For the collapse: give the description `<col>` a `min-w-[10rem]` and drop `table-fixed`, or switch to the card layout under ~480px of container width rather than viewport width.
Impeccable: `adapt`.

**P2 — No discard inside Match manually.**
What: after any picker change the only exit is save (`match-manually.tsx:77-81`).
Fix: second button "Discard changes" when `dirty`, Escape prompts if dirty, otherwise leaves.
Impeccable: `harden`.

## 7. Persona red flags

- **AP reviewer, 80 invoices before lunch**: every mismatched row snaps the layout and hides the source; each `≠` needs a mouse click to read; no shortcut to jump to the next `≠` or to toggle View PO (`line-items-section.tsx:130`). The PO facet "Mismatch" helps triage; the row's three coloured counts do not. Chip clicks navigate away with no Origin.
- **Controller approving on a phone**: the bottom sheet is right and reachable; the green band and Reject PO sit in thumb reach. But the `=`/`≠` glyph is 24×24px (`GLYPH_BASE`, `po-compare.tsx:17`) — the WCAG floor, not a comfortable target; the Purchase Orders column is off-screen on the 390 list (`invoices-list-390.png`), so a phone controller cannot see which invoices have a PO problem without opening each. Every meaning carried by `title` is unavailable to them. (Context only: the incumbent pane header uses ~45 % of the phone viewport before the tabs.)
- **Keyboard / screen reader**: solid bones — named glyph buttons, `role="switch"`, focus to the breakdown's close and back, Escape, heading focus on entering Match manually, per-row `aria-label`ed selects. Gaps: the chip count is a `span` with `aria-label` (`po-compare.tsx:196`) — unreliable without a role; the glyph lacks `aria-expanded`; "by hand" (`line-items-editor.tsx:166`) and "PO removed"'s meaning are `title`-only; the PO-pane "over" note is `hidden` text inside the cell (`po-consumption-panel.tsx:44`) which is fine for SR but nothing visual says "over" beyond red.

## 8. Minor observations

- Amount column shows no PO line under it while its neighbours do (`invoice-pane-viewpo-1440.png`) — reads as an omission; a muted "—" or `not compared` would close the gap.
- Description gets a green `=` for a 71 % similarity guess; equal sign overstates a fuzzy match. Consider a different glyph or none for description, keep `=` for numeric cells.
- Chip jumps right when the View PO toggle unmounts on entering Match manually (`line-items-section.tsx:130`); the Done label changing width also shifts.
- PO list: "Invoiced $1,794 115 %" in red while "Consumption: Open" — true but reads contradictory; add "20 remaining on 1 line" or show the over line count.
- PO pane "Delivery 1 / 1" digits appear tinted blue in `po-pane-1440.png` — verify no link styling leaks into the cell.
- Received column of dashes on the PO queue is a decided column (#228 Q8) — rendering could at least mute the header and put "Not recorded" once, not a "—" per row.
- Breakdown mixes two bases: "22 % over what was ordered" then "Over by 17" (over the allowance). One extra row "Over ordered by 22" would remove the arithmetic the reader does in their head.

## 9. Copy

- **"PO No PO line"** (`line-items-editor.tsx:92` + `:136` prefix) → drop the "PO" prefix for that case: "No PO line".
- **Pill vocabulary** (`po-compare.tsx:33-35`): "Matches" / "Mismatch" / "Not compared" / "Not matched" — inconsistent grammar and the last two are near-identical. Glossary says a line below threshold "has no line match and is not compared", so the no-PO-line state should read **"Not compared"** and the has-PO-line-but-no-values state needs another word (e.g. "Nothing to compare"). Consider "Match" / "Mismatch" as the Check-status pair.
- **"Pick a PO line for each row below"** (`match-manually.tsx:85`) — rows are prefilled; "Change the PO line on any row below" is what actually happens.
- **"…or fix the match."** (`line-items-section.tsx:42`) → "…or change the match in Match manually." — use the glossary name.
- **"3 mismatches"** (pane header) vs **"3 cells do not match the PO"** (tooltip) vs 2 "Mismatch" pills — pick "cells" everywhere or say "2 lines and the total".
- **Column "Purchase Orders"** (`invoice-queue.tsx:122`) for one chip per row, facet **"PO"** (`:55`) — use "PO" for both, matching the chip text.
- **"Not this one"** (`match-manually.tsx:98`) vs **"Reject PO"** (`:114`) — two verbs for rejecting; acceptable if intentional (suggestion vs link), but "Not this one" has no noun and a screen-reader user hears it without the PO number.
- **"Remaining 0"** when 22 over (`po-consumption-panel.tsx:45`) → "0 · 22 over".
- **"Consumption: Open"** beside "115 %" — add what remains, or the facet label "Open" reads as a mistake.
- **"Comparing against … — confirmed."** is good; **"— matched by the PO number on the invoice, not yet confirmed."** is good.
- **Dashed chip title** "Suggested by the matcher; nothing is compared until it is confirmed in Match manually" is the clearest sentence on the surface and is hidden in a tooltip — surface it in the Match manually band's suggested state text (`match-manually.tsx:87`), which currently says only "No PO is compared yet. Confirm a likely PO below, or choose another."

Add a small caret or a 2px emerald edge on the side facing the glyph.

- **"Consumption: Open"** beside "115 %" — add what remains, or the facet label "Open" reads as a mistake.

- **Dashed chip title** "Suggested by the matcher; nothing is compared until it is confirmed in Match manually" is the clearest sentence on the surface and is hidden in a tooltip — surface it in the Match manually band's suggested state text (`match-manually.tsx:87`), which currently says only "No PO is compared yet. What: chip "3", header "3 mismatches", but two "Mismatch" pills; the third `≠` (Total) is below the fold (`line-items-section.tsx:58-62`).
Why: the decided rule is "the red count equals the number of `≠` the pane shows" — it is true in code and false in the viewport.
Fix: chip tooltip and header wording → "3 cells · 2 lines + Total"; or scroll the Total's compare line into view when View PO auto-opens; or mirror the Total's `≠` beside the chip.
Impeccable: `clarify`.

**P2 — View PO hides the source, and the suggested state leaves an unreadable table.**
What: comparing flips the pane to details-only (`line-items-section.tsx:102-107`); when there is only a suggestion, nothing widens and at 1440-split the fixed-width table collapses its description column and overprints headers ("DESCRIPTIQUANTITY", `invoice-pane-suggested-1440.png`; `line-items-editor.tsx:225-230`).
Why: the reviewer needs the invoice image beside the PO values; and the suggested-PO row is the one where they most need to read the descriptions to decide.
Fix: keep split at ≥1280 and let the table scroll horizontally with a sticky description column; below that, widen. For the collapse: give the description `<col>` a `min-w-[10rem]` and drop `table-fixed`, or switch to the card layout under ~480px of container width rather than viewport width.
Impeccable: `adapt`.

**P2 — No discard inside Match manually.**
What: after any picker change the only exit is save (`match-manually.tsx:77-81`).
Fix: second button "Discard changes" when `dirty`, Escape prompts if dirty, otherwise leaves.
Impeccable: `harden`.

## 7. Persona red flags

- **AP reviewer, 80 invoices before lunch**: every mismatched row snaps the layout and hides the source; each `≠` needs a mouse click to read; no shortcut to jump to the next `≠` or to toggle View PO (`line-items-section.tsx:130`). The PO facet "Mismatch" helps triage; the row's three coloured counts do not. Chip clicks navigate away with no Origin.
- **Controller approving on a phone**: the bottom sheet is right and reachable; the green band and Reject PO sit in thumb reach. But the `=`/`≠` glyph is 24×24px (`GLYPH_BASE`, `po-compare.tsx:17`) — the WCAG floor, not a comfortable target; the Purchase Orders column is off-screen on the 390 list (`invoices-list-390.png`), so a phone controller cannot see which invoices have a PO problem without opening each. Every meaning carried by `title` is unavailable to them. (Context only: the incumbent pane header uses ~45 % of the phone viewport before the tabs.)
- **Keyboard / screen reader**: solid bones — named glyph buttons, `role="switch"`, focus to the breakdown's close and back, Escape, heading focus on entering Match manually, per-row `aria-label`ed selects. Gaps: the chip count is a `span` with `aria-label` (`po-compare.tsx:196`) — unreliable without a role; the glyph lacks `aria-expanded`; "by hand" (`line-items-editor.tsx:166`) and "PO removed"'s meaning are `title`-only; the PO-pane "over" note is `hidden` text inside the cell (`po-consumption-panel.tsx:44`) which is fine for SR but nothing visual says "over" beyond red.

## 8. Minor observations

- Amount column shows no PO line under it while its neighbours do (`invoice-pane-viewpo-1440.png`) — reads as an omission; a muted "—" or `not compared` would close the gap.
- Description gets a green `=` for a 71 % similarity guess; equal sign overstates a fuzzy match. Consider a different glyph or none for description, keep `=` for numeric cells.
- Chip jumps right when the View PO toggle unmounts on entering Match manually (`line-items-section.tsx:130`); the Done label changing width also shifts.
- PO list: "Invoiced $1,794 115 %" in red while "Consumption: Open" — true but reads contradictory; add "20 remaining on 1 line" or show the over line count.
- PO pane "Delivery 1 / 1" digits appear tinted blue in `po-pane-1440.png` — verify no link styling leaks into the cell.
- Received column of dashes on the PO queue is a decided column (#228 Q8) — rendering could at least mute the header and put "Not recorded" once, not a "—" per row.
- Breakdown mixes two bases: "22 % over what was ordered" then "Over by 17" (over the allowance). One extra row "Over ordered by 22" would remove the arithmetic the reader does in their head.

## 9. Copy

- **"PO No PO line"** (`line-items-editor.tsx:92` + `:136` prefix) → drop the "PO" prefix for that case: "No PO line".
- **Pill vocabulary** (`po-compare.tsx:33-35`): "Matches" / "Mismatch" / "Not compared" / "Not matched" — inconsistent grammar and the last two are near-identical. Glossary says a line below threshold "has no line match and is not compared", so the no-PO-line state should read **"Not compared"** and the has-PO-line-but-no-values state needs another word (e.g. "Nothing to compare"). Consider "Match" / "Mismatch" as the Check-status pair.
- **"Pick a PO line for each row below"** (`match-manually.tsx:85`) — rows are prefilled; "Change the PO line on any row below" is what actually happens.
- **"…or fix the match."** (`line-items-section.tsx:42`) → "…or change the match in Match manually." — use the glossary name.
- **"3 mismatches"** (pane header) vs **"3 cells do not match the PO"** (tooltip) vs 2 "Mismatch" pills — pick "cells" everywhere or say "2 lines and the total".
- **Column "Purchase Orders"** (`invoice-queue.tsx:122`) for one chip per row, facet **"PO"** (`:55`) — use "PO" for both, matching the chip text.
- **"Not this one"** (`match-manually.tsx:98`) vs **"Reject PO"** (`:114`) — two verbs for rejecting; acceptable if intentional (suggestion vs link), but "Not this one" has no noun and a screen-reader user hears it without the PO number.
- **"Remaining 0"** when 22 over (`po-consumption-panel.tsx:45`) → "0 · 22 over".
- **"Consumption: Open"** beside "115 %" — add what remains, or the facet label "Open" reads as a mistake.
- **"Comparing against … — confirmed."** is good; **"— matched by the PO number on the invoice, not yet confirmed."** is good.
- **Dashed chip title** "Suggested by the matcher; nothing is compared until it is confirmed in Match manually" is the clearest sentence on the surface and is hidden in a tooltip — surface it in the Match manually band's suggested state text (`match-manually.tsx:87`), which currently says only "No PO is compared yet. Confirm a likely PO below, or choose another."

CONTEXT.md:20:The one cross-type lookup: a Queue screen whose rows are every document in the workspace that matches what was typed — any type, any processing state, archived included — with nothing listed until something is typed. Its rows open in the Detail pane in place; a typed row also offers to open on its own queue, which is a hop that carries Origin context. Documents of a type that has no queue of its own (contracts, delivery notes, payslips, tax forms, other) are found and opened here and nowhere else. Reached from the rail and, on desktop, the `/` key.
CONTEXT.md:163:**Origin context**:
CONTEXT.md:164:The workspace, list, filters, position, and workflow state from which a user opened a detail or action surface — in DocuBite, the origin surface's address as it stood, including the selected row. It exists only for a **hop**: an in-app link that opens a row on a *different* surface (an Invoices row to its Exception, a Search result to its typed queue, a failed ledger push to its document, the Detail pane to its full-width page). Opening a row's Detail pane on the same queue, and choosing a queue from the rail, are not hops and carry nothing. Origin context lives exactly as long as the navigation that carries it: using the Origin link, the browser's Back, or any rail link ends it; nothing is remembered for the session. Returning restores the origin whenever it still exists; when the row no longer matches the origin's filters, the queue says so and offers to show the row instead of silently dropping it.
CONTEXT.md:167:**Origin link**:
CONTEXT.md:168:The one visible way back from a hop: a single strip above the arrival surface's header that names the origin surface and the row or search it will restore (*← Back to Invoices · Acme Corp · INV-1042*). It renders only while an Origin context exists, agrees with the browser's Back, and is the only control that crosses surfaces — the Detail pane's × and Escape close the pane on the current queue and never leave it.
